title: Material Formation of Recombinant Spider Silks through Aqueous Solvation using Heat and Pressure
protocol: Reconstitute recombinant spider silk mixture from lyophilized protein stocks.
Determine the necessary formulation and volume required for intended material formations.
Calculate appropriate concentrations and ratios of MaSp1:MaSp2 based on formulations.
Use 6% (w/v) MaSp1:MaSp2 ratio for hydrogels/sponges/lyogels.
Use 5% (w/v) MaSp1:MaSp2 ratio for films/coatings.
Use 12% (w/v) MaSp1:MaSp2 ratio for adhesives.
Use 12.5% (w/v) MaSp1:MaSp2 ratio for fibers.
Select a clean and new 8 mL autoclavable borosilicate glass culture vial with rubber-lined screw cap.
Remove the cap from the selected vial.
Place the empty vial on an analytical balance.
Tare the mass of the empty vial to zero.
Add desired lyophilized rSSp powder to the empty vial for specific material.
Weigh 60 mg of MaSp1 and 60 mg of MaSp2 for hydrogels/sponges/lyogels.
Add ultrapure water, at least 2 mL, to the vial containing weighted rSSp powders.
Seal the vial cap and vortex briskly to create a dispersed, homogenous mixture.
Transfer the suspended rSSp mixture to a conventional microwave oven for solvation.
Perform a final check of the vial cap to ensure it is firmly tightened.
Operate the microwave with 5 s bursts at full power.
Briefly open the door and mix/swirl the vial after each burst to prevent settling and maintain suspension.
Repeat the process until the mixture reaches a temperature of at least 130 °C, as measured by an infrared thermometer.
Continue heating until all solid particulates are completely dissolved and no longer visible.
Allow the vial and solution to cool occasionally if high concentration of rSSp is present.
Ensure that temperatures do not exceed 200 °C to prevent vial seal failure.
Prevent superheated mixture from touching the vial seal to avoid containment failure.
Wait until both the solution temperature and the vial cap temperature drop below 100 °C before opening.
Prepare a hydrogel from the cooled solution after removing it from the microwave.
Cast the hydrogel into specific geometries prior to full cooling.
Allow the primary solvated rSSp solution to form a hydrogel.
Place the formed hydrogel in a water bath and place this bath in the freezer at -20°C until completely frozen.
Remove the frozen hydrogel and water bath from the freezer, thawing at 25°C.
Remove the resultant sponge from the thawed water bath.
Directly freeze a formed hydrogel, either with or without a water bath.
Transfer the frozen hydrogel sample to a lyophilizer (freeze dryer).
Remove the final lyophilized gel material from the vessel used for sublimation.
Cast the solubilized rSSp solution into/onto PDMS forms of desired shape.
Pour 200 µL of the film solution.
Spread the poured solution evenly.
Allow the spread solution to dry completely.
Peel off the dried films from the PDMS substrate for testing or treatment.
Prepare a coating by using spray or dip coating methods on the chosen substrate.
Spray coat the substrate using a master airbrush model paint sprayer.
Form a dip coating by submerging the substrate into the solubilized rSSp solution and drying after each dipping to achieve desired thickness.
Perform an initial spray coat before applying a dip coat to enhance consistency and effectiveness of the final coating.
Directly add the solubilized rSSp onto a substrate surface.
Apply a second substrate over the top of the rSSp layer and clamp firmly together.
Dry the assembled samples in an oven at a minimum temperature of 25 °C for at least 16 hours.
Spray both substrate surfaces with rSSp solution using a spray coating method.
Clamp the sprayed substrates together to form an adhesive.
Apply the rSSp through dip coating on each substrate surface before sticking them together to prepare an adhesive.
Load the solubilized dope solution into a concentric syringe with Luer-Lok tip through a 19 G glide needle.
Eject air bubbles from the syringe.
Insert at least 25 mm of PEEK tubing, internal diameter 0.01 inch, into one-piece finger tight fittings for 1/16 inch OD and 10/32 cone.
Attach the fitting to a PEEK tubing to Luer-Lok female adapter.
Replace the 19 gauge needle with the set up on the loaded syringe.
Fill a tall, clear glass bath with 99% pure isopropanol for coagulation bath.
Fill the first stretch bath with 80:20 isopropanol: distilled water.
Fill the second stretch bath with 20:80 isopropanol: distilled water.
Set the godet stretch system such that the first godet after the coagulation bath and the first godet in the first stretch bath are rotating at the same speed.
Initiate the first stretch by adjusting the speeds of the final godet in stretch bath 1, the middle upper godet, and the first godet in stretch bath 2 to the same speed.
Adjust the speed for the first stretch to be twice as fast as the initial fiber removal speed.
Initiate the second stretch by adjusting the speeds of the final godet in stretch bath 2, the last upper godet, and the winder to the same speed.
Set the speed for the second stretch to be twice as fast as the speed used for the first stretch or four times the initial fibers removal speed.
Place nitrile gloves on the outside of the intermediate godets to keep the fiber from slipping.
Slowly extrude the solution into the coagulation bath.
Set the extrusion rate to match a removal speed of 10 mm/s in an automated system.
Allow fiber extrusion to become uniform before pulling fibers out of the bath using a thin metal hook or forceps.
Verify that removing the fiber from the bath created a loop between the PEEK tubing tip and the path the fiber leaves the bath.
Guide the retrieved fiber through the series of godets such that the fiber is submerged in the stretch baths but drying in the air between the baths.
Attach the fully stretched fiber to the spool on the winder mechanism using tape.
